messages:
Anya K.: Quick flag — after flipping INT4 for nova-lite on the 'priming' slice we observed a 5-7% drop in top-3 exact-match for multi-turn primed prompts. Noticing it in both eval harness and a small prod sample.
Ben L.: ugh. do we have the slice + a couple of failing examples?
Anya K.: yep. sample metrics (priming_slice_v2):
```
INT8 baseline: top3=0.82, MRR=0.61
INT6 trial: top3=0.80, MRR=0.60
INT4 rollout: top3=0.76, MRR=0.56
```
Top-3 drop concentrated on long primed contexts (>= 1k tokens).
Sara P.: is this a decoding artifact or quantization noise in KV cache? 
Mike R.: my money is on KV/attention quantization for long context. INT4 sometimes messes up key/value precision which compounds over long priming.
Anya K.: here are two raw prompts that flipped from correct->wrong (redacted):
- "Prompt A" -> expected answer snippet present in priming context but model omitted it
- "Prompt B" -> hallucinated shorter answer, lost grounding
Ben L.: can you paste the diff of logits/top-k for the tokens around the anchor where it goes wrong? even small probability shuffles can break exact-match.
Anya K.: pasted a tiny diff excerpt:
```
Token idx 45: INT8 p(correct)=0.23 -> INT4 p=0.11
Token idx 46: INT8 p(alt)=0.12 -> INT4 p=0.18
```
Ben L.: ok that supports the hypothesis. two quick asks: 1) repro on a fresh container with deterministic seed, 2) run INT4 but disable KV-cache to see if it's KV-related.
Anya K.: running now. also kicking off INT6 run to check monotonic degradation.
deploy-bot: canary deploy 2024-06-14T15:02:12Z - model=nova-lite-int4 - rollout=10%
Sara P.: also check prompt tokenization differences between runs (we chopped a token earlier in preprocessing patch). could be orthogonal but worth verifying.
Mike R.: if disabling KV fixes it, we can short-term fallback to INT6 for primed routes and keep INT4 for short-single-turn to keep cost wins. routing flag idea: route by max_context_tokens > 512 -> INT6/INT8, else INT4.
Ben L.: agreed. let's quantify cost delta so product/GTN can decide. rough calc: INT4 avg cost per token = 0.18x INT8; INT6 ~0.55x. If we route <512 tokens to INT4 and >=512 to INT6, projected cost saving ~23% vs INT8 on this workload (approx). need formal numbers.
Anya K.: I'll generate a micro-scorecard: per-slice accuracy, delta cost, tail-latency impact, and an A/B plan. aim to have by EOD.
Sara P.: add an inclusion test: run a 1k-sample of multi-turn priming with `disable_kv=true` + INT4 and compare. include priming fidelity metric (presence recall).
Mike R.: also want a quick kernel-level trace for matmul quant paths; file it with eng-runtime if we see non-linear error growth across steps. cc @eng-runtime later.
Ben L.: perfect. action items:
- Anya: reproduce (deterministic) + micro-scorecard (EOD)
- Anya: run INT4 w/ KV disabled + INT6 baseline (in progress)
- Sara: tokenization sanity check on preprocessing (low effort)
- Mike: prepare kernel trace request if repro shows compounding error
- Ops: pause further INT4 canaries until triage done (deploy-bot you can throttle)

Anya K.: noted. will ping with the scorecard link when ready. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Ben L.: thanks — if we confirm KV root, routing fix + fallback should be a low-risk mitigation. :thumbsup:
Sara P.: if routing is implemented, product/GTN needs a short blurb on expected cost delta + UX risk so they can communicate to customers.
Mike R.: agreed. we'll keep the rollback plan simple (route all primed routes to INT6) until we have a proper int4-KV patch.
Anya K.: update 20m later: INT4 w/ KV disabled recovers ~90% of the drop (top3=0.80). INT6 baseline sits at 0.81. so KV quantization is almost certainly the culprit.
Ben L.: great signal. can you attach the detailed numbers in the scorecard? I'll draft the routing flag PR.
Anya K.: will do. attaching soon.
deploy-bot: canary throttle applied - model=nova-lite-int4 - rollout set to 0%
Mike R.: nice. we'll proceed with routing + retention of INT4 for short contexts.
Sara P.: thanks team. let's sync tomorrow if any new surprises.
